title: Pool cleaning start-up essentials and licence status checklist
audience: People planning to start a pool cleaning or maintenance service in Australia, and supervisors checking their readiness
learningOutcomes: List the equipment, vehicle, paperwork and office items a pool service needs before its first visit
Identify each start-up step in the US guide and state whether it applies in Australia, with its status
Explain that a course certificate or a registration number is not a licence and must not be implied by the business documents
Complete a start-up readiness list in which every regulatory item is marked as checked or still to be checked

instruction.heading: What a pool service needs before its first job
instruction.body: The US start-up guide lists the basic items a pool service carries: pool cleaning tools, the chemical products for pool treatment, a vehicle large enough to carry supplies, business cards, invoices, contract forms, a diary, a laptop and a printer. Those practical items apply in Australia too. Add a test kit for sanitiser and pH, a net and skimmer, a vacuum and hoses, brushes, spare seals, and the storage needed to keep chemicals apart from each other and from the vehicle's fuel and from people. The vehicle must carry the chemicals securely.

instruction.heading: The licence step: not applicable as written
instruction.body: The US guide tells the reader to find out which business licence is needed at the local council office. It also says that a licence protects the business legally, lets it buy supplies at trade prices, and makes clients more inclined to hire. Those points describe US local government and US practice, and they do not apply in Australia. In Australia the registration, licence or competence needed for pool work depends on the state or territory, the council, the kind of pool and the task. This lesson grants no licence and no registration, and it should never be read as implying either.

instruction.heading: Pool operator courses are not a licence
instruction.body: The US guide describes several training courses for pool operators and technicians, and it lists their fees and certificate terms. Those courses, their certificates, their fees and their validity periods are US-specific. None of them is used or endorsed here. Their names are not repeated as recommendations. Completing any course in Australia is not, by itself, a licence or an authority to operate a pool. See “Licences, permissions and restricted work” for the general licence rules.

instruction.heading: Finding staff and telling people about the service
instruction.body: The US guide suggests hiring through local advertisements, through friends and family with pool experience, and by using additional help once the business grows. The guide also suggests delivering business cards to acquaintances, approaching apartment communities, condominium managers, real estate agents and banks that hold properties with pools, and advertising in local newspapers. “Marketing, referrals and retention for pool service work” covers the marketing plan.

instruction.heading: Readiness list
instruction.body: Before the first job, list each item in four groups: practical equipment, vehicle and storage, paperwork and office items, and regulatory status. Every regulatory item is marked either as checked with the source and date, or still to be checked. A start-up is ready only when every equipment item is in place and every regulatory item is either checked or marked clearly as still to be checked, with a named person responsible for confirming it.

procedure: List the practical equipment and chemicals the planned services need.
List the vehicle and storage requirements, including separation of chemicals and secure carriage.
List the paperwork and office items, including the invoice, contract and calendar.
For each US guide step, mark it as applicable, not applicable, or still to be checked for Australia.
Name the authority that will confirm each regulatory item and the date it was checked.
Record the readiness list and the person who signed it off.

workedExamples.situation: A new operator plans to start a pool service next month and says their course certificate is enough to carry out chemical treatment for any client.
workedExamples.reasoning: A course certificate is not a licence or an authority to treat water for a client. Record the request, mark the treatment work as not yet permitted, and refer to the licence checks.

workedExamples.situation: The owner plans to keep chemicals in the back of a personal car with a fuel can, because the vehicle is the only storage available.
workedExamples.reasoning: Advise against it. Chemicals must be kept apart from each other and from fuel and people, and the vehicle must carry them securely. Record the advice.

equipmentAndPpe: Test kit for sanitiser and pH with reagents in date
Net, skimmer, brushes, vacuum head, pole and hoses
Secure storage for chemicals, separated by type
Vehicle or trailer sized for the supplies
Invoice book or invoice template, contract forms and calendar

commonErrors.error: Treating a course certificate as a licence
commonErrors.prevention: Check the licence or registration status with the authority, and leave it blank until checked.

commonErrors.error: Copying US licence or course advice into Australian business papers
commonErrors.prevention: Mark every US statement as not applicable and replace it with the Australian check.

commonErrors.error: Storing chemicals with fuel or in the cabin
commonErrors.prevention: Store chemicals separated, secured and away from fuel and people.

commonErrors.error: Starting work before the readiness list is signed off
commonErrors.prevention: Complete the readiness list and name the person who confirms each item.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The US guide's licence advice is not applicable in Australia.
This lesson grants no licence, registration, certificate or authority to treat water, handle dangerous goods or operate a pool.
US pool operator courses, fees and certificates are not applicable to Australia and are not endorsed.
Carriage and storage of pool chemicals in vehicles are subject to dangerous goods rules, so check with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.
Check employment, insurance and advertising rules with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.

qualityStandard: Every equipment and storage item on the list is in place or marked as not yet obtained.
Every US guide step is marked applicable, not applicable or still to be checked.
No regulatory item is marked as confirmed without a source and a check date.
documentationEvidence: Signed readiness list with each item's status
Source and date for each regulatory check made
Record of the person responsible for confirming each item still to be checked
summary: A pool service needs practical equipment, safe storage and clear paperwork before its first visit.
A course, certificate or registration number is not a licence, and US licence rules do not apply in Australia.
Every regulatory item stays out until it is checked against an Australian authority.

knowledgeChecks.question: A new operator says a training course certificate lets them treat water for any client. What is the correct response?
options: Agree, because a certificate is a licence and it covers every pool in the state, every client and every chemical
Explain that a certificate is not a licence, and that the Australian requirement has not yet been confirmed until checked
Tell them the US rules apply in Australia too and the local council will not mind any of the work done
Advise them to start treating water and check later and sign the client's agreement before they begin

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about the US start-up guide's licence advice is correct for Australia?
options: It applies once a business has at least one client and the client has paid the first invoice
It applies in full because the guide is published and the US authority has approved it
It is not applicable, and the Australian requirement must be checked with the relevant authority
It applies only in the state of the reader and only to pools with a heater fitted in the yard

knowledgeChecks.question: How should chemicals be carried and stored in a service vehicle?
options: Together in the cabin, for convenience with the client's own tools and the spare parts
Beside the fuel can, to save space and close to the driver's seat and the lunch box
Loose in the tray so they can be reached quickly with the lids off during the drive
Separated by type, secured, and away from fuel and people, with the Australian rules checked
